entries.title: Filter generation in practice: from algorithms to LLMs
entries.description: We automate filter generation for security alerts using an algorithm, a large language model, and a group of LLM agents.

entries.title: Unknown APT uses NetamLoader to attack a Win10 OS customized for governments in Asia
entries.description: Kaspersky researchers analyze a complex targeted attack employing NetamLoader, a sophisticated malicious framework and targeting a customized government OS.

entries.title: LABScon26 Replay | Keynote: A Sober Analysis of AI Impact
entries.description: Harvard Professor James Mickens weighs the promises of AI against its potential harms, arguing for hardware-based mechanisms to isolate frontier models.

entries.title: Millions of security cameras at risk: DoS vulnerability in Intelbras devices
entries.description: During our research, we discovered a denial-of-service vulnerability that could affect millions of Intelbras IP camera systems built on the platform platform of a popular Chinese manufacturer.

entries.title: Tricks from the Past deployed via signed ChatGPT and Claude binaries
entries.description: Over the past two months, we have been tracking a campaign that abuses the popularity of AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude to spread a custom malware chain we call Yoba . The attackers use fake GitHub projects that pretend to be AI desktop applications like GPT-5.6 Sol , GPT-6 Astra , and Claude Opus . These projects look convincing and use real GitHub infrastructure, which helps them appear legitimate to potential victims. The website exhibits search-targeted content and suspicious installer-

entries.title: An insecure neighbor: how a vulnerability chain led to an isolation bypass in cloud infrastructure
entries.description: A Kaspersky expert presents a cloud isolation bypass case honored at Russian Pentest Award 2026. Learn how vulnerabilities in Kubernetes, Konnectivity, and the overlay network lead to RCE and compromise of other tenants' services.

entries.title: 26th October – Threat Intelligence Report
entries.description: For the latest discoveries in cyber research for the week of 26th October, please download our Threat Intelligence Bulletin.

entries.title: Deploying AI agents securely: how Kaspersky products mitigate AI threats
entries.description: We look at best practices for deploying AI tools securely in corporate environments, with Kaspersky Security Center and Kaspersky Endpoint Security as examples. We also cover ways that EDR and TIP can detect AI agents.

entries.title: Kernel eviction notice: What wesp.sys reveals about the Windows Endpoint Security Platform
entries.description: Microsoft wants EDR out of the Windows kernel, and the preview binaries show wesp.sys telling a user-mode client that a process is starting, with nothing in its imports to let that client block it.

entries.title: Infostealer riding the AI Train
entries.description: Infostealers commonly target browser passwords, session cookies, and cryptocurrency wallets. This malware combines those established capabilities with dedicated collection routines for AI applications and development tools. Its targets include Claude, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, and GitHub Copilot, alongside cloud credentials and sensitive files from local development environments.

entries.title: How CVE-2026-73570 turns a Zimbra log file into remote code execution
entries.description: We reproduced the Zimbra command injection vulnerability and found that several public PoCs write a payload Swatchdog never matches, so a failed test looks like a patched server.

entries.title: How APT41 revived the BlackLotus bootkit to attack diplomatic organizations in Central Asia
entries.description: Kaspersky GReAT experts discovered a new UEFI bootkit, BlackX. It exploits the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894) and is similar to the BlackLotus bootkit.

entries.title: Critical RCE vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
entries.description: We discuss the incident involving the leak of information about vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Kaspersky solutions detect the PHP2Shell exploit: we’ll walk you through examples using KEDR, KATA, and KES.

entries.title: Operation FlashHole: Lazarus breaks security, defies control
entries.description: Kaspersky researchers analyze Operation FlashHole – a recent complex attack by Lazarus, involving a sophisticated malware set, watering-hole technique and abuse of CrossWeb EX financial security software.

entries.title: php2shell: Assessing Elastic detection coverage relevant to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
entries.description: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are critical PHP core RCE flaws that leaked ahead of disclosure. We cover what is verified, why exploitation converges on a web server spawning a shell, and the Elastic detections developed to catch this behavior.

entries.title: The Risk of AI-Powered Antidetect Browsers in Online Fraud and Influence Operations
entries.description: Antidetect browsers conceal their users’ digital identities, enabling a single operator or small team to simultaneously run thousands of isolated accounts across multiple platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Twitter/X, Discord, LinkedIn, Reddit, and many more, without triggering the detection systems employed by those platforms.

entries.title: The journey of a paper unicorn: adventures inside a modern warehouse
entries.description: Kaspersky experts explain the security issues affecting warehouse environments. We break down initial access vectors specific to warehouses, and discuss the impact of a compromise.

entries.title: When LLM Gateways Go Wrong: Findings from LiteLLM
entries.description: As LLM gateways see wider adoption, understanding the security risks they introduce is essential to deploying them safely within an AI stack. These systems sit between applications and model providers and often handle credentials, configuration, and request routing. We decided to take a closer look at LiteLLM, one of the most popular LLM gateways in use today. entries.title: Auditing the auditor: Unmasking Apex Accelerator
entries.description: REF8801 exposes how Apex Accelerator combines convincing Web3 services with malicious npm packages, attacker-controlled AI infrastructure, and cross-platform malware delivery.

entries.title: Introducing AlertZero: Inbox zero for your alert queue
entries.description: AlertZero brings AI SOC automation to Elastic Security with four agents, one job each, so the queue stops setting your priorities. Nothing changes in your environment without your approval.

entries.title: Behind the tags: How Elastic SIEM grades 1,781 detection rules on noise, speed, and threat coverage
entries.description: This article explains how Elastic SIEM uses a monthly automated telemetry pipeline to score prebuilt detection rules across noise, performance, threat, and profile dimensions, helping security teams decide which rules to enable first.
